title: Reading the Signals
briefing: Amara Lindqvist, Fleet Manager, has had three in-transit temperature excursions in a quarter and two drivers' hours breaches last month. Her monthly pack reports deliveries, fuel spend and on-time delivery, and none of it warned her.
Priya has asked you to design key risk indicators that would give early warning, set thresholds, and agree what happens when one turns amber.

context.text: After the Eastfield compressor failure, the COO has asked for early warning instead of post-mortems. This work now has an audience.
Site sign-off for contractor visits now produces a weekly report you could also use as an indicator.
Amara mentions that Kelvarin's contract rolled over unchanged. She is not convinced the risk team changes anything.

evidence.title: Fleet monthly pack (current indicators)
body: Deliveries completed: 41,200 (up 3%). Fuel spend: 1.21m (up 6%). On-time delivery: 96.2%.
No indicator has a threshold or an owner. The pack is read at the monthly operations meeting.

evidence.title: In-transit temperature excursions, last quarter
body: Three excursions above 8C. All three were on routes planned for more than 9 hours of driving, two of them on the final drop of the day.
Each was found when the data logger was downloaded at the depot, between 1 and 3 days after delivery.

evidence.title: Drivers' hours (tachograph) extract
body: Breaches of daily driving limits: 0, 0, 1, 2 in the last four months. 38 per cent of routes are now planned above 9 hours, up from 22 per cent a year ago.

evidence.title: Board risk appetite (extract)
evidence.body: Valtren has no appetite for food safety breaches and a low appetite for regulatory breaches. Operational disruption is tolerated within budget.

questions.prompt: Which indicator gives the earliest warning of in-transit temperature excursions?

options.label: Share of routes planned above 9 hours of driving
options.feedback: A leading indicator: it moves before excursions do, and all three excursions were on long routes.

options.label: Number of excursions per quarter
options.feedback: Worth tracking, but it is lagging: it counts the harm after it has happened.

options.label: Deliveries completed
options.feedback: A volume measure, not a risk signal.

options.label: Fuel spend
options.feedback: A cost measure with no link to the risk.

questions.prompt: Which indicators belong on the new fleet risk dashboard?

options.label: Share of data loggers downloaded within 24 hours of delivery
options.feedback: This also shortens the 1-3 day delay in finding excursions.

options.label: Share of routes planned above 9 hours
Total deliveries completed
options.feedback: Volume is not a risk indicator.

options.label: Fuel litres per month
options.feedback: No link to the appetite statement or to the excursions.

questions.prompt: What thresholds do you set for drivers' hours breaches per 1,000 shifts?

options.label: Amber at 1, red at 3, reviewed after one quarter
options.feedback: Above zero to avoid constant alarms, well below where a regulator would act, and reviewed once there is data.

options.label: Red at any breach
options.feedback: Matches the appetite wording but every month would be red: people stop reacting to an alarm that is always on.

options.label: Amber at 10, red at 20
options.feedback: Far too loose: at 2,000 shifts a month this would allow 40 breaches before red.

options.label: No thresholds; just show the trend
options.feedback: Without thresholds nobody knows when to act.

questions.prompt: The long-route share has been amber for two weeks running. What do you do?

options.label: Escalate to Amara as the KRI rule requires, with a proposal to split the two longest routes, and log an action with a due date
options.feedback: The rule exists so that people act before red. You escalated to the owner with a fix.

options.label: Wait: amber is not red yet
options.feedback: An amber that nobody acts on is decoration. The fatigue risk kept growing.

schedules.description: A tired driver clips a barrier on a 10-hour route; the load is lost

options.label: Order all routes cut below 8 hours from Monday (40,000 in extra vehicles)
options.feedback: Not your call to make or fund, and an overnight change risks missed deliveries.

questions.prompt: How do you present the indicators to the operations meeting?

options.label: One page: each indicator with its threshold, trend, owner and the agreed action when it turns red
A detailed workbook with every route's data
options.feedback: Useful for analysis, not for a meeting that must decide.

options.label: Show only indicators that are red
options.feedback: Hiding amber removes the early warning you just designed.

lesson: Good indicators lead the harm, have thresholds tied to appetite and an owner, and come with an agreed action. An amber nobody acts on is decoration.
